reason: E3 directly supports that severe lattice distortion in multi-principal element alloys creates heterogeneous strain fields that enhance mechanical properties, but it does not address thermal expansion mismatch or cold rolling effects. E1 concerns a different alloy system (Ti-Nb-Mo-Sn) and attributes modulus changes to phase transformations, not lattice distortion amplification, so it does not support the key premises. E2 discusses short-range order effects on dislocation mobility in bcc RHEAs but does not provide evidence for lattice distortion amplification by thermal mismatch or cold rolling.
premises: Lattice distortion in HfNbTaTiZr creates local strain fields that impede dislocation mobility
Temperature-induced thermal expansion mismatch amplifies these lattice distortions
Cold rolling enhances lattice defects and thus amplifies distortion effects
Amplified distortions cause higher yield strength, work hardening, and elastic modulus variation
Diffraction techniques can isolate lattice distortion contributions from other microstructural effects
